best_for: Synth players and sound designers who want to patch a Eurorack-style modular on a computer for free, and who would pay for Pro only when they need Rack inside a DAW.

points.title: Free runs on its own
points.text: Rack Free is a standalone app with the free modules and community support. You patch cables between virtual modules on screen, so you can learn modular synthesis without buying hardware.

points.title: The DAW plugin is the paid line
points.text: Running Rack as a VST2, VST3, Audio Unit or CLAP plugin needs Rack Pro, listed at USD 149 (USD 129 until December 1). The plugin handles up to 16 audio and 16 MIDI inputs and outputs. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: VCV+ rents the premium modules
points.text: VCV+ costs USD 29 per month, or USD 19 per month paid yearly, and bundles Rack Pro with premium VCV and third-party modules. If you cancel, patches that use those modules go silent until you renew; Rack Free and modules you bought outright stay.

points.title: A large module library
points.text: VCV lists 30+ built-in modules, 170+ official hardware-clone modules and 2000+ modules in the VCV Library. Third-party `.vcvplugin` files can be dropped into the plugins folder, and the plugin's major version has to match Rack's.

points.title: It wants a real graphics card
points.text: The listed minimum is a 64-bit Intel or AMD CPU with SSE4.2 or an Apple M1 or later, 1 GB of RAM and 1 GB of disk. VCV recommends a dedicated Nvidia or AMD card from 2013 or later and says integrated Intel HD graphics are not recommended.

points.title: Older versions on Windows only
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 7 versions as a machine-wide 64-bit installer. macOS lists only the current universal .pkg, so going back on a Mac needs another source. VCV also offers a Linux build, which is not listed here.
